1. 🏛️ RBI POLICY, MASTER DIRECTIONS & PRUDENTIAL NORMS #

MONETARY POLICY COMMITTEE № 1

Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) — Benchmark Rate Corridor Trajectory

  • Continuous Policy Rate Pause: The MPC held the Policy Repo Rate at 5.25% with a neutral monetary stance across four consecutive bi-monthly reviews through the August 3–5, 2026 meeting (next review scheduled for Oct 5–7, 2026).
  • Standing Facility Rate Structure: Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) fixed at 5.00% (Repo - 25 bps); Marginal Standing Facility (MSF) and Bank Rate fixed at 5.50% (Repo + 25 bps); Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) holds at 3.00%; Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR) holds at 18.00%.
  • Statutory MPC Composition: 6-member committee under Section 45-ZB of the RBI Act, 1934; comprises 3 RBI officials (Governor Sanjay Malhotra as Chairperson, Deputy Governor, Executive Director) and 3 external government-appointed experts.
  • Live Macroeconomic Projections: MPC revised India's FY27 real GDP growth projection up to 6.7% (from 6.6%), while trimming FY27 CPI inflation projection down to 5.0% (from 5.1%).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Corridor Math): Repo = 5.25%, SDF = 5.00%, MSF/Bank Rate = 5.50% (SDF is always 25 bps below Repo; MSF is 25 bps above). • Trap B (Stance Confusion): Monetary stance is NEUTRAL (not 'Withdrawal of Accommodation'). • Target MCQ Form: "What is the Standing Deposit Facility (SDF) rate following RBI's August 2026 Monetary Policy Committee review?" → 5.00%.
DISPATCH № 2

Digital Fraud Compensation: Responsible Business Conduct (Third Amendment) Directions

  • Genesis & Compensation Slabs: Framed to protect victims of small-value, unauthorized electronic banking transactions (losses up to ₹50,000); mandates compensation of 85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is lower.
  • Institutional Loss-Apportionment Formula: For losses below ₹29,412, the 85% payout is apportioned: RBI bears 65% (funded via Depositor Education and Awareness / DEA Fund), the customer's issuing bank bears 10%, and the beneficiary bank bears 10%.
  • Statutory Deferred Effective Date: Formally notified in the Gazette on June 24, 2026, but RBI deferred enforcement to January 1, 2027 (pushed from the original July 1, 2026 draft date) to give banks integration runway.
  • Zero Customer Liability Principle: Guarantees zero liability where digital fraud occurs due to bank negligence or third-party breaches reported by the customer within 3 working days.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (The Date Trap): Implementation date is January 1, 2027 (do NOT pick July 1, 2026). • Trap B (The Cap Trap): Compensation is 85% of loss or ₹25,000, whichever is LOWER (not ₹50,000). • Target MCQ Form: "Under the RBI Responsible Business Conduct Directions, what is the mandatory effective date for the small-value digital fraud compensation framework?" → January 1, 2027.
DISPATCH № 3

Bank Dividend Payout Cap Overhaul: Graded CET1 Capital Architecture

  • Dismantling Legacy Cap: RBI dismantled the rigid decades-old regulation that strictly capped commercial bank dividend distributions at a uniform 40% of Profit After Tax (PAT).
  • Graded Capital-Linked Ceiling: Operational from FY26 balance sheets, maximum dividend payout is raised up to 75% of PAT for commercial banks maintaining a Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio ≥ 13.0%.
  • Foreign Bank Branch Remittances: Foreign banks operating in India via branch mode are permitted to remit up to 80% of net post-tax profits to head offices abroad, provided local Capital Conservation Buffers are met.
  • Asset Quality Barrier: A bank is statutorily disqualified from declaring dividends if its Net Non-Performing Assets (NNPA) ratio exceeds 6.0% for the financial year.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Domestic vs Foreign Cap): Domestic commercial bank max cap is 75%; Foreign bank branch remittance cap is 80%. • Trap B (NNPA Barrier): Net NPA must not exceed 6.0% for dividend eligibility. • Target MCQ Form: "What is the maximum dividend payout ratio permitted for domestic commercial banks having a CET1 ratio of 13% or higher?" → 75% of PAT.
DISPATCH № 4

Bank Acquisition Financing & Unlisted Target Guidelines

  • Prudential Bank Exposure Cap: RBI raised the bank exposure ceiling for acquisition financing from 10% to 20% of Tier-1 capital; permitted commercial banks to fund acquisitions of unlisted target companies.
  • Target Company Eligibility: Target unlisted firm must have a net worth ≥ ₹500 crore, a 3-year continuous track record of profitability, and minimum BBB- credit rating.
  • Financing Share & Security Margins: Permissible bank financing share raised to 75% of acquisition value (from 70%), with debt-equity ratio capped at 3:1; raised lending against shares to ₹1 crore (from ₹20 lakh).
  • Implementation Deferral: Enforcement officially deferred to July 1, 2026 (from original April 1, 2026); permitted corporate borrowing via Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) backed by mandatory Corporate Guarantees.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Effective Date): Acquisition financing directions took effect on July 1, 2026 (deferred from April 1). • Trap B (Promoter Funding Share): Maximum bank financing share is 75% of transaction value (promoter margin 25%). • Target MCQ Form: "What is the minimum net worth required for an unlisted target company to be eligible for bank acquisition financing?" → ₹500 Crore.
DISPATCH № 5

REIT & InvIT Bank Lending Regulatory Framework

  • Credit Opening for Investment Trusts: Permitted scheduled commercial banks to extend credit facilities to Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Infrastructure Investment Trusts (InvITs).
  • Prudential Exposure Ceilings: A single bank's exposure to an individual REIT/InvIT is capped at 10% of the bank's eligible capital base.
  • Aggregate Banking System Ceiling: The combined banking system exposure across all lenders to a single REIT/InvIT cannot exceed 49% of the gross asset value of the trust.
  • Enforcement Timeline: Fully operationalized across commercial banking books effective July 1, 2026.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Individual vs Aggregate Cap): Single bank cap is 10% of eligible capital; Aggregate banking system cap is 49% of trust asset value. • Trap B (Effective Date): Effective date is July 1, 2026. • Target MCQ Form: "Under RBI norms, what is the maximum aggregate exposure permitted for the entire banking system to a single REIT?" → 49% of the REIT's asset value.
DISPATCH № 6

Unprecedented Liquidity Operations: First-Ever 90-Day VRR Auction

  • Historical Tenor Breakthrough: On January 30, 2026, RBI conducted its first-ever 90-day Variable Rate Repo (VRR) auction for ₹25,000 crore, breaking the previous longest historical liquidity tenor of 56 days.
  • Package Components: Formed part of an aggregate ₹2.15 lakh crore liquidity intervention, including a $10 billion 3-year USD/INR Buy-Sell Swap and ₹1 lakh crore in Open Market Operation (OMO) purchases.
  • Bilateral Currency Stability: Renewed the $75 billion Bilateral Swap Arrangement (BSA) with the Bank of Japan, signed under Governor Sanjay Malhotra and BoJ leadership.
  • Policy Objective: Anchored short-term money market rates near the 5.25% repo rate amid massive advance tax and GST cash drains.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Tenor Record): The historic auction tenor was 90 days (previous high was 56 days). • Trap B (Bilateral Swap Size): India-Japan Bilateral Swap Arrangement is $75 billion. • Target MCQ Form: "What was the tenor of the historic long-term Variable Rate Repo auction conducted by the RBI in early 2026?" → 90 days.
POLICY • FLAGSHIP SCHEMES № 7

Lead Bank Scheme (1969) Overhaul: 60% Credit-Deposit Ratio Mandate

  • Statutory Credit-Deposit (CD) Mandate: Draft overhaul mandated a minimum Credit-Deposit (CD) ratio of 60% across all rural and semi-urban districts nationwide.
  • Special Category Districts: Districts recording a CD ratio below 20% are statutorily classified as 'Special Category Districts', requiring quarterly District Consultative Committee (DCC) monitoring.
  • Historical Committee Heritage: Lead Bank Scheme was originally introduced in 1969 following the recommendations of the F.K.F. Nariman Committee and the Study Group chaired by Prof. D.R. Gadgil.
  • Nodal Role: State Level Bankers' Committee (SLBC) and Lead District Manager (LDM) supervise credit flow to agriculture and allied rural sectors.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (CD Ratio Thresholds): Rural/semi-urban CD ratio mandated at 60%; special category threshold is below 20%. • Trap B (Committee Origin): Lead Bank Scheme was recommended by the Nariman Committee (1969). • Target MCQ Form: "Under the revised Lead Bank Scheme directions, what minimum Credit-Deposit ratio must banks maintain in rural and semi-urban districts?" → 60%.

RBI Annual Report 2025-26: Balance Sheet & Surplus Transfer to Centre

  • Record Balance Sheet Expansion: RBI's balance sheet expanded by 11.08% YoY to reach ₹70.47 lakh crore, driven by foreign exchange asset accumulation and domestic gold reserves.
  • Record Dividend / Surplus Transfer: Approved a record surplus transfer of ₹2.11 lakh crore to the Central Government for FY26 (cushioning the Union fiscal deficit).
  • Contingency Risk Buffer (CRB): Maintained the Contingency Risk Buffer within the recommended Economic Capital Framework (ECF / Bimal Jalan Committee) band at 6.50%.
  • Reserve Asset Composition: Foreign currency assets and sovereign gold reserves constitute over 72% of total balance sheet assets.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Rupee Figures Pair): Balance sheet size = ₹70.47 lakh crore; Surplus transfer to Centre = ₹2.11 lakh crore. • Trap B (Committee Name): Reserve transfer framework is governed by the Bimal Jalan Committee (2019). • Target MCQ Form: "What was the total surplus transfer approved by the RBI Board to the Central Government for FY26?" → ₹2.11 Lakh Crore.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 9

RBI Financial Stability Report (FSR): Banking System Asset Quality

  • Multi-Year Low Gross NPA: Scheduled Commercial Banks' (SCB) Gross Non-Performing Asset (GNPA) ratio dropped to 2.8% (the lowest level in 12 years); Net NPA fell to 0.6%.
  • Capital Adequacy Strength: Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) of scheduled commercial banks stood at a robust 16.8%, well above the Basel III regulatory minimum of 11.5% (including CCB).
  • Provision Coverage Ratio (PCR): System-wide Provision Coverage Ratio rose to 76.4%, indicating comprehensive provisioning against legacy bad debts.
  • Macro Stress Testing: RBI's baseline stress tests project system-level GNPA to remain stable below 3.0% under projected macroeconomic scenarios.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (GNPA vs NNPA): Gross NPA is 2.8%; Net NPA is 0.6% (do not invert the two figures). • Trap B (CRAR Level): Commercial bank CRAR is 16.8% (regulatory minimum is 11.5%). • Target MCQ Form: "According to the RBI Financial Stability Report, what was the multi-year low Gross NPA ratio recorded by Scheduled Commercial Banks?" → 2.8%.
DISPATCH № 10

Domestic Systemically Important Banks (D-SIBs) & Capital Surcharges

  • Identified D-SIB Entities: Reserve Bank of India re-affirmed State Bank of India (SBI), HDFC Bank, and ICICI Bank as Domestic Systemically Important Banks ("Too Big To Fail").
  • Tiered Additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) Surcharges:
    • Bucket 4 (SBI): Required to maintain an additional CET1 capital surcharge of 0.80% of Risk-Weighted Assets
    • Bucket 2 (HDFC Bank): Required to maintain an additional CET1 surcharge of 0.40% of RWAs
    • Bucket 1 (ICICI Bank): Required to maintain an additional CET1 surcharge of 0.20% of RWAs
  • Statutory Framework: Formulated under the D-SIB framework introduced in 2014, requiring systemic lenders to hold higher loss-absorbency capital.
  • Foreign G-SIB Analogue: Foreign bank branches operating in India designated as G-SIBs must hold corresponding additional capital buffers in India.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (The Capital Surcharges): SBI = 0.80% (Bucket 4), HDFC Bank = 0.40% (Bucket 2), ICICI Bank = 0.20% (Bucket 1). • Trap B (Total D-SIBs): Exactly 3 banks (SBI, HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank). • Target MCQ Form: "What additional Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital surcharge is State Bank of India required to maintain as a Bucket 4 D-SIB?" → 0.80%.
DISPATCH № 11

Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) Framework for Commercial Banks & NBFCs

  • Three Mandatory Risk Threshold Parameters: RBI monitors regulated financial institutions across three diagnostic financial metrics: (1) Capital (CRAR & CET1), (2) Asset Quality (Net NPA ratio), and (3) Leverage (Tier-1 Leverage Ratio).
  • Breach Threshold Slabs:
    • Risk Threshold 1: Triggered if Net NPA exceeds 6.0% (mandatory restriction on dividend payout and profit repatriation).
    • Risk Threshold 2: Triggered if Net NPA exceeds 9.0% (mandatory restriction on branch expansion).
    • Risk Threshold 3: Triggered if Net NPA exceeds 12.0% (mandatory restriction on capital expenditure and management compensation).
  • NBFC Inclusion: Extended to Middle, Upper, and Top-Layer NBFCs under Scale-Based Regulation to prevent systemic shadow-banking defaults.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (PCA Trigger Parameters): Capital, Asset Quality (Net NPA), and Leverage (Profitability/RoA was REMOVED as a trigger). • Trap B (Threshold 1 Net NPA): Threshold 1 is breached at 6.0% Net NPA. • Target MCQ Form: "Which of the following financial parameters is NO LONGER a primary trigger for invoking the RBI Prompt Corrective Action framework?" → Return on Assets (RoA).
DISPATCH № 12

Scale-Based Regulation (SBR) for NBFCs & Upper Layer (Tata Sons Mandate)

  • Four-Layer Regulatory Architecture:
    • Base Layer (NBFC-BL): Assets < ₹1,000 crore
    • Middle Layer (NBFC-ML): Assets ≥ ₹1,000 crore
    • Upper Layer (NBFC-UL): Top 25 identified systemic entities or assets ≥ ₹1 lakh crore
    • Top Layer (NBFC-TL): Activated only under extreme contagion risk (currently empty)
  • Tata Sons Designated Upper-Layer: Classified as NBFC-UL for 2026-27; subject to enhanced regulatory scrutiny for a mandatory minimum of 5 years regardless of subsequent asset changes.
  • Mandatory Listing Requirement: NBFC-UL entities are statutorily required to list their equity shares on recognized stock exchanges within 3 years of being categorized.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Asset Slabs): Base Layer (<₹1,000 Cr) ➔ Middle Layer (≥₹1,000 Cr) ➔ Upper Layer (≥₹1 lakh Cr / Top 25). • Trap B (Enhanced Regulation Duration): Upper-Layer regulations apply for a mandatory minimum of 5 years; listing within 3 years. • Target MCQ Form: "Under RBI Scale Based Regulation, what is the asset threshold for categorizing an NBFC into the Middle Layer?" → ₹1,000 Crore.
DISPATCH № 13

External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) Liberalised Guidelines

  • Automatic Route Borrowing Cap: RBI raised the automatic borrowing limit under the ECB framework to the higher of $1 billion or 300% of borrower net worth per financial year (escalated from $750 million).
  • Corporate Borrowing Boom: Indian corporate entities raised a record $61 billion via ECBs in FY25, driven by global refinancing and renewable capex lines.
  • Minimum Average Maturity Period (MAMP): Retained at 3 years for general commercial borrowings, and 5 years for borrowings by manufacturing companies up to $50 million.
  • End-Use Restrictions: ECB proceeds strictly prohibited from being deployed in real estate equity trading, capital market speculation, or domestic on-lending.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Annual Cap): Automatic ECB cap is the higher of $1 billion or 300% of net worth (raised from $750 million). • Trap B (MAMP): Minimum Average Maturity Period is 3 years for standard ECBs. • Target MCQ Form: "What is the revised annual borrowing limit for Indian corporates under the automatic route of the RBI ECB framework?" → $1 Billion or 300% of Net Worth.
DISPATCH № 14

Unique Trade Identifier (UTI) Mandate for OTC Financial Derivatives

  • Mandatory Reporting Directive: RBI mandated the generation and reporting of Unique Trade Identifiers (UTIs) for all Over-the-Counter (OTC) interest rate, foreign exchange, and credit derivative transactions.
  • Statutory Effective Date: Full mandatory compliance enforced effective January 1, 2027.
  • Regulatory Reporting Repository: All derivative transactions must be reported to the Clearing Corporation of India Ltd (CCIL) Trade Repository within specified settlement cutoffs.
  • Global Financial Stability Convergence: Aligns domestic derivative market oversight with G20 and Financial Stability Board (FSB) technical commitments.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Effective Date): Mandatory UTI reporting takes effect on January 1, 2027. • Trap B (Trade Repository): Derivative reporting repository is managed by CCIL (Clearing Corporation of India Ltd). • Target MCQ Form: "From which date has the RBI made Unique Trade Identifiers (UTIs) mandatory for all Over-the-Counter derivative contracts?" → January 1, 2027.

RBI Digital Payments Index (DPI) & Sovereign Gold Reserves

DISPATCH № 17

Positive Pay System (PPS) for Cheque Truncation System (CTS)

  • Fraud Prevention Mechanism: Mandates electronic re-confirmation of key cheque details (date, payee name, amount) before clearing high-value instruments under the Cheque Truncation System (CTS).
  • Monetary Confirmation Thresholds:
    • Voluntary / Recommended Threshold: Applicable for cheques valued at ₹50,000 and above.
    • Mandatory Bank Discretion Threshold: Banks may make confirmation mandatory for cheques valued at ₹5 lakh and above.
  • Dispute Redressal Protection: Cheques cleared without Positive Pay confirmation are disqualified from grievance redressal under CTS dispute mechanisms.
  • Continuous Clearing Grid (2026): RBI initiated round-the-clock continuous clearing of cheques under CTS, reducing clearance turnaround from T+1 days to a few hours.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Thresholds Pair): ₹50,000 (discretionary threshold) vs ₹5 Lakh (mandatory threshold set by most banks). • Trap B (Dispute Rule): Cheques issued without Positive Pay confirmation cannot be disputed under CTS dispute resolution. • Target MCQ Form: "At what cheque transaction threshold is the Positive Pay System generally made mandatory by commercial banks?" → ₹5 Lakh and above.
DISPATCH № 18

UDGAM Portal & Unclaimed Deposits in DEA Fund

  • UDGAM Portal Launch: RBI deployed UDGAM (Unclaimed Deposits – Gateway to Access inforMation), enabling public users to search for unclaimed savings, current, and term deposits across multiple commercial banks on a single platform.
  • Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund: Unclaimed deposits transferred to the DEA Fund surged to ₹86,917.08 crore (as of June 30, 2026), with State Bank of India holding the highest unclaimed volume (~₹16,000 crore).
  • Unclaimed Deposit Rule: Any savings or current account inoperative for 10 years, or any term deposit unclaimed for 10 years from the date of maturity, must be transferred to the DEA Fund.
  • Interest Refundability: Depositors retain the statutory right to reclaim their funds along with interest directly from the bank at any future date.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Unclaimed Time Period): Account must be inoperative/unclaimed for 10 years before transfer to the DEA Fund. • Trap B (Portal Acronym): UDGAM = Unclaimed Deposits – Gateway to Access inforMation. • Target MCQ Form: "After how many years of remaining inoperative must balances in bank accounts be transferred to the RBI Depositor Education and Awareness (DEA) Fund?" → 10 Years.
DISPATCH № 19

Centralised Information Management System (CIMS) Big-Data Architecture

  • Next-Gen Data Warehouse: RBI fully operationalized the Centralised Information Management System (CIMS), phasing out the legacy Online Returns Filing System (ORFS).
  • Automated Regulatory Reporting: Deploys automated straight-through data feeds (APIs) from commercial banks and NBFCs, performing real-time algorithmic supervisory risk audits.
  • Governor Launch: Commissioned under Governor Shaktikanta Das and expanded under Governor Sanjay Malhotra, handling petabytes of structured banking transaction data.
  • XBRL Phase-Out: Completely replaces eXtensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL) reporting returns with unified, automated data pipes.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Replaced System): CIMS replaces ORFS (Online Returns Filing System) and XBRL platforms. • Trap B (Full Form): CIMS = Centralised Information Management System. • Target MCQ Form: "Which next-generation data warehouse system was operationalized by the RBI to replace the legacy Online Returns Filing System (ORFS)?" → CIMS.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 20

RBI Draft (Interest Rates on Loans and Advances) Directions, 2026

  • Harmonized Principles-Based Code: Released on August 12, 2026 for public consultation, unifying fragmented interest rate directives across commercial banks, cooperative lenders, and NBFCs.
  • Fair Practices in Reset Frequency: Mandated transparent disclosure of benchmark rate resets; prohibited arbitrary penal interest rates, restricting penalties strictly to penal charges (not capitalized into principal loan balances).
  • Key Fact Statement (KFS) Mandate: Made comprehensive Key Fact Statements mandatory for all retail and MSME loans, disclosing Annual Percentage Rate (APR) and all associated processing fees upfront.
  • Floating Rate Loan Switching: Regulated entities must provide floating-rate borrowers an explicit option to switch to a fixed-rate loan or adjust loan tenor upon interest rate hikes.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Penal Charges Rule): Penalties must be levied as penal charges and cannot be capitalized (cannot earn additional interest). • Trap B (KFS Universal Scope): Key Fact Statement is mandatory for ALL retail and MSME loans. • Target MCQ Form: "Under RBI's Fair Lending Practice guidelines, how must lenders levy penalties for loan defaults?" → As separate penal charges (without adding to principal).

2. 🏦 BANKING, CREDIT FACILITIES & FINANCIAL INCLUSION #

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 21

DICGC Four-Tier Risk-Based Premium Architecture

  • Transition to Risk-Sensitive Pricing: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) transitioned from the legacy flat premium of 12 paise per ₹100 of assessable deposits to a four-tier risk-based premium model effective April 1, 2026.
  • Supervisory Risk Slabs:
    • Category A (Safest): 8 paise per ₹100
    • Category B: 9 paise per ₹100
    • Category C: 10 paise per ₹100
    • Category D (Highest Risk): 12 paise per ₹100
  • Insurance Coverage Ceiling: Statutory deposit protection remains locked at ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (covering principal and interest across all domestic branches).
  • Statutory Foundation: Enacted under the DICGC Act, 1961; DICGC operates as a 100% subsidiary of the Reserve Bank of India.

    • SMA-0: Principal or interest payment not overdue for more than 30 days, but showing signs of incipient stress.
    • SMA-1: Overdue for 31 to 60 days.
    • SMA-2: Overdue for 61 to 90 days (pre-NPA warning bucket).
    • NPA: Overdue for more than 90 days.
  • Weekly Reporting of Defaults: Regulated lenders must report defaults of ₹5 crore and above on a weekly basis to CRILC.

DISPATCH № 36

  • Inward Remittance & Merchant Acceptance: Enables Indian travelers to make direct QR-based payments in local currencies, and Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) to remit funds instantly to Indian bank accounts without SWIFT delays.
  • P2P and P2M Transaction Volume Scale: UPI handled over 14.44 billion transactions in a single calendar month (exceeding ₹20.64 lakh crore in value), cementing India's status with >45% of global real-time digital payments.

  • ₹5 Lakh Special Transaction Slab: Enhanced limit of ₹5 Lakh applies to: (1) Hospitals and Medical Healthcare, (2) Educational Institutions, (3) Direct and Indirect Tax Payments, and (4) IPO and Capital Market Retail Subscriptions.

UPI CIRCLE № 38

UPI Circle — Delegated Payments Architecture for Family Accounts

  • Secondary User Authorization: NPCI launched 'UPI Circle', enabling a primary bank account holder to authorize a trusted secondary user (family member, dependent, child) to execute payments from the primary account.
  • Two Delegation Modalities:
    • Full Delegation: Primary user establishes a monthly spending cap (maximum ₹15,000 per month), allowing the secondary user to spend autonomously within limits without secondary approval.
    • Partial Delegation: Secondary user initiates the payment request, but each transaction requires final biometric or PIN authorization from the primary user.
  • Security Guardrails: Primary user can link a maximum of 5 secondary delegates and revoke authorization in real time.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Monthly Cap): Under Full Delegation, the maximum monthly spending limit set by the primary user is ₹15,000 (not ₹25,000). • Trap B (Delegate Count): A primary user can authorize up to 5 secondary delegates. • Target MCQ Form: "What is the maximum monthly transaction limit permissible under the 'Full Delegation' mode of NPCI's UPI Circle?" → ₹15,000.

Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC) — Sovereign e-Rupee Innovations

  • Dual Pilot Architecture: RBI operates two distinct pilots: e₹-W (Wholesale) launched Nov 1, 2022 (interbank settlement of secondary G-sec transactions and call money market) and e₹-R (Retail) launched Dec 1, 2022.
  • Programmability & Offline Capabilities: Enabled programmable e-Rupee tokens with targeted end-use (e.g., direct benefit transfer for agricultural input subsidies, school fee vouchers) with automated expiry dates and merchant geofencing.
  • UPI Interoperability: e₹-R wallets can scan any standard interoperable UPI QR code, enabling consumers to spend digital rupees at over 30 million merchant touchpoints nationwide.

  • Lowered Entry Thresholds:

    • Minimum application size slashed from ₹2 Lakh to ₹10,000, democratizing retail and philanthropic participation.

RBI Peer-to-Peer (P2P) Lending NBFC Regulatory Crackdown

  • Prohibition of Guarantees: Master Directions explicitly barred NBFC-P2Ps from marketing P2P loans as alternative high-yield investment products with credit enhancement, assured returns, or liquidity guarantees.
  • Lender & Borrower Exposure Caps:
    • Aggregate exposure of a lender across all P2P platforms capped at ₹50 Lakh (investments >₹10 Lakh require net-worth certificate from a Chartered Accountant).
    • Aggregate borrowing of a single borrower across all P2P platforms capped at ₹10 Lakh.
  • Tenure Ceiling: Maximum loan maturity on P2P platforms restricted to 36 months.
  • Fund Flow Rigor: Mandates T+1 escrow settlement; platforms cannot hold funds in their own balance sheet or provide revolving credit lines.

Capital Gains Taxation Architecture: Dual Rationalization

Wholesale Price Index (WPI) & Consumer Price Index (CPI) Structural Anchors

  • Base Year Parameters:
    • Consumer Price Index (CPI - Combined): Base Year is 2012=100; published monthly by the National Statistical Office (NSO), MoSPI.
    • Wholesale Price Index (WPI): Base Year is 2011-12=100; published monthly by the Office of the Economic Adviser, DPIIT, Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
  • Weightage Distribution Traps:
    • CPI Weights: Food & Beverages = 45.86%; Housing = 10.07% (urban only); Fuel & Light = 6.84%; Miscellaneous = 28.32%.
    • WPI Weights: Manufactured Products = 64.23%; Primary Articles = 22.62%; Fuel & Power = 13.15% (Note: Services are completely excluded from WPI).
  • Inflation Targeting Metric: Under Section 45-ZA of the RBI Act, the official inflation target of 4% (±2% tolerance band) is legally bound to CPI-Combined, NOT WPI.

8. ⚖️ REGULATORY BODIES, ACTS, COMMITTEES & APPOINTMENTS #

DISPATCH № 100

Telecommunications Act, 2023 Enacted into Law

  • Century-Old Law Repeal: Formally repealed archaic colonial legislations: the Indian Telegraph Act, 1885, the Indian Wireless Telegraphy Act, 1933, and the Telegraph Wires (Unlawful Possession) Act, 1950.
  • Administrative Allocation of Satellite Spectrum: Mandated the administrative allocation of satellite communication spectrum (satcom) without competitive auctioning, aligning India with global ITU standards for Starlink, Eutelsat OneWeb, and Jio Satellite.
  • Digital Bharat Nidhi: Renamed and restructured the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) into 'Digital Bharat Nidhi' to support R&D, pilot deployment, and rural broadband expansion.
  • Biometric SIM Guardrails: Enforces mandatory biometric verification for SIM acquisition, prescribing penalties up to ₹50 Lakh and 3 years imprisonment for fraudulent acquisition using forged identities.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Satellite Spectrum Allocation): Allocated ADMINISTRATIVELY, not through public auction. • Trap B (Renamed USOF): USOF was renamed to Digital Bharat Nidhi. • Target MCQ Form: "Under the Telecommunications Act 2023, the Universal Service Obligation Fund (USOF) was renamed as which entity?" → Digital Bharat Nidhi.
DISPATCH № 101

Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act, 2023 Regulatory Framework

  • Statutory Genesis & DPBI: Establishes the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI) as an autonomous digital adjudicatory authority to investigate breaches and impose statutory penalties.
  • Penalties Slabs:
    • Failure to prevent significant personal data breach: Penalties up to ₹250 Crore.
    • Failure to fulfill duties of Data Fiduciary towards children: Up to ₹200 Crore.
    • General non-compliance penalties: Up to ₹50 Crore.
  • Consent Architecture: Introduces the legal concept of 'Consent Managers' registered with the DPBI, interoperable consent withdrawal, and mandatory notice in all 22 Eighth Schedule languages.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Maximum Penalty): Maximum penalty for failing to prevent a significant data breach is ₹250 Crore per instance. • Trap B (Adjudicating Body): Governed by the Data Protection Board of India (DPBI). • Target MCQ Form: "What is the maximum financial penalty that can be imposed under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 for failure to prevent a personal data breach?" → ₹250 Crore.
DISPATCH № 102

Criminal Justice Overhaul: BNS, BNSS & BSA Operationalization

  • Enforcement Date: Came into full legal effect across India on July 1, 2024, completely replacing the British-era penal codes.
  • Three Replaced Statutes:
    1. Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023 replaced the Indian Penal Code (IPC), 1860.
    2. Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), 2023 replaced the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC), 1973.
    3. Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023 replaced the Indian Evidence Act, 1872.
  • Pioneering Legal Reforms:
    • Introduction of Zero FIR (can be registered at any police station regardless of jurisdiction).
    • Mandatory audio-video recording of search and seizure operations.
    • Introduction of Community Service as a recognized punishment for petty offenses.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE [THE EXAMINER'S TRAP MATRIX] • Trap A (Enforcement Date): Enacted into law on July 1, 2024 (not Jan 1 or April 1). • Trap B (Law Mapping): BNS = IPC; BNSS = CrPC; BSA = Evidence Act. • Target MCQ Form: "On which date did the three new criminal laws (BNS, BNSS, and BSA) come into legal force across India?" → July 1, 2024.

POLICY • FLAGSHIP SCHEMES № 12

GOBARdhan: Fuelling Clean Energy and Rural Growth — full scheme detail 🔄 UPDATE (PIB 1–10 Aug backgrounder, merged with the entry above)

  • Full form: Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan; approved by Union Cabinet 6 August 2026; Nodal Ministry MoPNG; originally launched 2018 under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen), Solid & Liquid Waste Management component
  • Core concept: converts cattle dung, agri residue, press mud, municipal/kitchen/market organic waste into Compressed Biogas (CBG) — chemically equivalent to natural gas — and organic manure
  • Six Growth Engines: (1) Assured CBG Offtake — CGD entities procure under a notified CBG Obligation trajectory: 3% FY 2026-27 → 4% FY 2027-28 → 5% from FY 2028-29 onwards in CNG (Transport)/PNG (Domestic) segments; (2) Stable Pricing — administered price ₹2,110/MMBTU (~₹105/kg); (3) Capital Assistance — up to ₹2 crore/TPD of installed CBG capacity for greenfield projects; (4) Pipeline Infrastructure — connects CBG plants to trunk pipelines & CGD networks; (5) Credit Guarantee — up to 85% coverage for eligible MSME-based CBG projects; (6) CBG Ecosystem Challenge Fund — feedstock mapping, aggregation, tech, district planning, manure value addition
  • Supporting initiatives: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation — promotes CBG production/supply to OMCs); Biomass Aggregation Machinery (BAM) Scheme — outlay ₹564.75 crore; Development of Pipeline Infrastructure (DPI) Scheme — outlay ₹994.5 crore, FY24-25 to FY28-29; MDA Scheme — Market Development Assistance for organic manure, ₹1,500/MT; CFA — Central Financial Assistance for CBG plants under National Bioenergy Programme
  • GOBARdhan Unified Registration Portal — registration required to avail MoPNG benefits/support
  • Top-performing states: 1. Uttar Pradesh → 2. Madhya Pradesh → 3. Maharashtra → 4. Gujarat → 5. Telangana; Top banks: 1. SBI → 2. BoB → 3. Union Bank of India → 4. PNB → 5. Indian Bank; Top ULB: Municipal Corporation of Delhi
  • 2026-36 expected outcomes: CBG 10×, fossil-fuel displacement 10 MMT, forex savings >₹40,000 cr, GDP addition >₹75,000 cr, >1.5 lakh jobs, CO₂ reduction >40 MT, organic fertilizer 250 MMT
🎯 EXAM ANGLE Six Growth Engines' CBG Obligation trajectory (3%→4%→5%) is a strong sequencing trap alongside the already-known ₹23,731 cr outlay; don't confuse GOBARdhan's original 2018 launch (under Swachh Bharat) with its 6 Aug 2026 Cabinet-approved revamp.

  • Release schedule: WPI, OPPI and Trial IPPI released on the 14th of the following month

POLICY • FLAGSHIP SCHEMES № 65

Tribunal Reforms Bill, 2026 — National Tribunals Commission (NTC) full composition 🔄 UPDATE (PIB 11–18 Aug backgrounder, merged with the NTDG entry above)

  • Passed by Parliament in August 2026 to make tribunals independent, transparent, efficient & uniform; repeals Tribunal Reforms Act, 2021; basis — SC directions in Madras Bar Association v. Union of India
  • NTC Composition: Chairperson (SC Judge/HC Chief Justice); Four Members — 2 Judicial Members (HC Chief Justice/HC Judge) + 2 Technical Members (25+ years' experience in public administration, finance, law, accountancy, banking, management or technology); appointment by Central Govt, after consultation with CJI for Chairperson & Judicial Members
  • NTC's 4 major functions: Selection, Review performance (monitor tribunals + annual reports), Inquiries, Data (→ National Tribunals Data Grid, covering the already-noted 16 tribunals)
  • Tenure: NTC Chairperson/Members — 5 years/age 70, whichever earlier; Tribunal Members — 5 years/age 67, whichever earlier; reappointment allowed based on previous service & performance
  • Search-cum-Selection Committees: for Chairperson selection — Committee Chair is the NTC Chairperson, plus 1 Technical Member, a retired HC Chief Justice, a GoI Secretary/State Chief Secretary (for SATs), 2 empanelled experts, and a Member Secretary; for Member selection — Committee Chair is the NTC Judicial Member, with an analogous composition (retired HC Judge instead of retired Chief Justice)
  • Key provisions: Committee Chair holds the casting vote; Member Secretary + 2 expert members have no voting rights; recommendation = 1 suitable candidate/vacancy + 1 for waiting list; Timeline — Secretariat must communicate recommendations to Central Govt within 3 days; Government must process and appoint within 3 months
🎯 EXAM ANGLE NTC's 2 Judicial + 2 Technical Member composition and the 3-day/3-month appointment timeline is a strong new-body MCQ, layering onto the already-logged NTDG (16 tribunals) fact.

CENTRALISED PUBLIC GRIEVANCE R... № 103

Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) — Samadhan Didi & NextGen upgrade (PIB 1–10 Aug)

  • Government's flagship digital public grievance-redressal platform, 24×7, connecting Central Ministries/Departments/States/UTs; evolved from a registration portal into an AI/analytics-driven governance platform
  • Under 2024 guidelines, grievances targeted for resolution within 21 days; Feedback Call Centre assesses satisfaction post-disposal; dissatisfied citizens can appeal to the Nodal Appellate Authority (30-day resolution window)
  • Improvement: annual grievances handled up ~9× to ~27 lakh (2024); average disposal time in Central Ministries fell to 15 days (2025)
  • Does not entertain: RTI matters, court/sub-judice matters, religious matters, govt-employee service matters (incl. disciplinary proceedings); supports 22 scheduled languages + English via BHASHINI; GRAI benchmarks Ministries/Departments; officer training under the Sevottam framework
  • Samadhan Didi — AI-enabled CPGRAMS voice chatbot, launched 30 May 2026; citizens speak their grievance in preferred language (AI + BHASHINI for speech-to-text/translation/transliteration)
  • NextGen CPGRAMS (upcoming): voice-enabled registration & chatbot, AI-based categorisation/routing, 22-language support, omni-channel registration
  • 10-Step Reform Programme introduced 2022 as the major evolutionary turning point
🎯 EXAM ANGLE CPGRAMS' 21-day resolution target vs its actual 15-day average disposal (2025) is a clean overshoot fact.

Samudra Manthan — National Offshore Exploration Scheme (PIB 1–10 Aug — standing exception, Template A regardless of zone)

🪝 Nearly all of India's previously "No-Go" offshore areas are now open for exploration under India's most ambitious offshore-oil mission yet.

  • Union Cabinet approved Samudra Manthan (India's most ambitious offshore exploration mission); Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas; Central Sector Scheme; Outlay ₹84,084 crore; Implementation up to FY 2030-31/31 March 2031; aim — reduce import dependence (India is world's 3rd-largest crude oil consumer), boost domestic O&G production
  • Components: Offshore seismic data acquisition & processing ₹28,534 cr; Accelerated deepwater exploration (60 wells) ₹43,200 cr; Common offshore infra hubs ₹10,000 cr; O&G Mfg/Services Zones + monitoring/support ₹2,350 cr (₹2,000 cr + ₹350 cr)
  • Govt support for deepwater drilling: up to 50% of eligible drilling cost or ₹675 crore/well, whichever is lower; focus basins — Krishna-Godavari, Cauvery, Mahanadi, Andaman; ~99% of previously restricted "No-Go" areas in India's EEZ opened for exploration
  • Key targets: domestic O&G production to 80 MMTOE annually; hydrocarbon resource base expansion to 2.2 billion TOE; potential crude-import reduction ~₹1 lakh crore annually
🎯 EXAM ANGLE Samudra Manthan's ₹84,084 cr outlay + 99% "No-Go" area opening is a near-certain mains question; don't confuse the ₹675 cr/well cap with the ₹84,084 cr total outlay.

Pradhan Mantri Viksit Bharat Rojgar Yojana (PM-VBRY) (PIB 1–10 Aug)

  • Objective: promote first-time employment, formal jobs, expand social security; announced August 2025; implementation 1 Aug 2025 – 31 July 2027 (2 years); outlay ₹99,446 crore; target >3.5 crore employment opportunities incl. 1.92 crore first-time employees; EPFO-linked digital platform; complements the National Manufacturing Mission
  • Part A (First-Time Employees): eligibility — earning up to ₹1 lakh/month; one-time incentive = one month's EPF wage, capped ₹15,000, paid in 2 instalments (after 6 months' service; after 12 months + financial-literacy completion); portion invested in a designated savings instrument
  • Part B (Employers): incentive up to ₹3,000/month per eligible additional employee, for 2 years (extended to 3rd/4th years for manufacturing sector)
  • One-year impact (Aug 2026): 72+ lakh first-time employees joined the formal workforce; ~30% beneficiaries are women
  • Digital governance: EPFO-linked platform, Aadhaar-based authentication, UAN, ECR filings, Face Authentication Technology on UMANG App, DBT to Aadhaar-linked accounts, PM-VBRY Portal; institutional mechanism — cross-functional teams from EPFO, ESIC, CLC (Chief Labour Commissioner)

MSME Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026 passed by Parliament (PIB 1–10 Aug)

  • Udyam-registered MSMEs: 9.16 crore; employment: 40+ crore people; focus — Ease of Doing Business, decriminalisation, formalisation, delayed-payment resolution
  • Makes Udyam Portal a permanent digital, free & voluntary registration platform
  • Court proceedings: mandates courts to order payment of at least 50% of the awarded amount to micro/small-enterprise suppliers if a set-aside application is pending 6+ months
  • Mediation to complete within 90 days of first appearance; arbitration reference within 30 days of mediation termination; arbitral award within 90 days of completion of pleadings
  • Recovery of dues (mediated settlement/arbitral award) recoverable as an "arrear of land revenue" via District Collector/Deputy Commissioner
  • TReDS: CPSEs mandated to route invoice settlements through it; invoice discounting rose to ₹3.47 lakh crore (2025-26)
  • States can establish multiple Micro and Small Enterprises Facilitation Councils (MSEFCs) and frame their own rules
  • Penalties: decriminalisation — conviction-based fines replaced by graded civil penalties

DISPATCH № 110

e-Samudra, e-Shram portal & PM-SYM cluster (PIB cluster)

  • e-Samudra — single-window digital maritime-governance platform, launched 8 August 2026 by Sarbananda Sonowal (Union Minister for Ports, Shipping & Waterways), Mumbai; shifts maritime administration to "Digital First and Faceless Governance"; incorporates e-NAVIK 24×7 grievance redressal, upcoming Seafarer Tracking Dashboard, Digital Seafarers Employment Agreement (d-SEA), enhanced Seafarers Welfare Fund Society (SWFS) measures
  • e-Shram Portal — launched 26 August 2021 by Ministry of Labour & Employment; creates a National Database of Unorganised Workers (NDUW) incl. platform/migrant/gig workers; registered workers get a Universal Account Number (UAN); self-declaration + Aadhaar eKYC; 31.82 crore+ unorganised workers registered; "One-Stop-Solution" (launched 21 Oct 2024) integrates 15 Central Government schemes
  • Pradhan Mantri Shram Yogi Maandhan (PM-SYM) — launched February 2019, Ministry of Labour & Employment; voluntary/contributory pension for unorganised-sector workers; assured pension ₹3,000/month after 60; eligibility — age 18-40, monthly income ≤₹15,000, not an EPFO/ESIC/NPS member or income-tax assessee; monthly contribution ₹55-₹200 (50% beneficiary + 50% Central Govt match); enrolment via Common Service Centres or maandhan.in; 54 lakh+ beneficiaries enrolled (29 July 2026), 53.1% women, Govt's matching contribution ₹2,011.01 crore; pension disbursement begins not before February 2039
🎯 EXAM ANGLE e-Samudra's "Digital First, Faceless Governance" tagline for maritime administration is a fresh standalone; PM-SYM's 2039 disbursement start (from a 2019 launch) is a clean date-arithmetic MCQ.

CBDT — Income-tax Rules, 2026 & "Kar Saathi" (merged: new rules + AI assistant launch)

🪝 Hook — CBDT slimmed 511 tax rules down to 333 and rolled out an AI chatbot, "Kar Saathi," to help taxpayers navigate the new Income Tax Act, 2025 regime — effective April 1, 2026.

  • Tax Year replaces 'Previous Year'/'Assessment Year'
  • Charitable trust record: retention cut from 10 → 6 years
  • Reliefs: children's education allowance ₹100 → ₹3,000/month (max 2 children); hostel allowance → ₹9,000; employer gifts exempt up to ₹15,000; meal exemption → ₹200/meal
  • HRA exemption expanded: to Hyderabad, Pune, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru (50% slab, previously only 4 metros)
  • PAN mandatory for: property deals only above ₹20 lakh (up from ₹10 lakh)
  • Kar Saathi — AI-enabled 24x7 taxpayer assistant, part of 'PRARAMBH 2026' (Policy Reform and Responsible Action for Mission Viksit Bharat) campaign
  • CBDT: HQ New Delhi | Chairman Ravi Agrawal | Formed 1944

💼 Interview Q → Why replace "Previous Year/Assessment Year" with a single "Tax Year"? → Simplifies compliance under the new Income Tax Act, 2025 by removing the dual-year confusion that often causes filing errors.

🪝 Hook — The MPC kept rates on hold for a second straight meeting, even as it penciled in a punchy 6.9% GDP growth forecast for FY27 amid West Asia tensions.

  • Real GDP Growth Projections: Projected real GDP growth for FY27 at 6.9% (quarterly path: Q1 at 6.8%, Q2 at 6.7%, Q3 at 7.0%, Q4 at 7.2%).

🎯 EXAM ANGLE Standing exception (always Tier A). Repo rate figure + all associated rates (SDF/MSF/CRR/SLR) are classic MCQ fodder.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 10

RBI — Two-Factor Authentication (2FA) Mandatory for Digital Payments

🪝 Hook — A single OTP will no longer cut it: from April 1, 2026, every UPI, card, and wallet transaction needs a second layer of verification.

  • Mandatory Two-Factor Scope: 2FA made compulsory across UPI, debit/credit cards, and prepaid mobile wallets — standalone SMS OTP is legally insufficient.
  • Secondary Factor Choices: Requires PIN, biometric fingerprint, hardware token, password, or facial recognition as the dynamic secondary authentication layer.
  • Institutional Liability Shift: Regulated banks and payment platforms held financially liable to compensate customers for unauthorized fraud losses arising from system vulnerabilities.
  • Staggered Compliance Timeline: Effective April 1, 2026; full enforcement across all merchant terminals and cross-border transactions mandated by October 2026.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE Effective date (Apr 1, 2026) vs full implementation date (Oct 2026) — classic date-confusion trap.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 11

RBI — Digital Payments Fraud Safeguards (Discussion Paper)

🪝 Hook — RBI's proposed fix for UPI fraud: force a one-hour "cooling-off" pause on big transfers, borrowing straight from the "golden hour" principle in crime prevention.

  • 1-hour cooling-off period proposed for A2A transfers above ₹10,000 (no chargeback option currently exists)
  • Data-Driven Fraud Threshold: Threshold chosen because ₹10,000+ transfers = ~45% of fraud cases by volume, ~98.5% by value
  • High-Value Secondary Verification: Transactions above ₹50,000 → additional verification (trusted-individual approval)
  • Mule account annual credit cap proposed at ₹25 lakh
  • New user controls: channel on/off toggle, custom limits, emergency "kill switch"

💼 Interview Q → What is the "golden hour" principle referenced by RBI? → The idea that the period immediately after a fraudulent transaction is most critical to prevent dissipation of funds — hence the proposed 1-hour delay window.

🎯 EXAM ANGLE ₹10,000 (cooling-off threshold) vs ₹50,000 (extra verification) vs ₹25 lakh (mule account cap) — three-number trap cluster.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 12

RBI — Digital Payments E-Mandate Framework, 2026

  • Registration Safeguards: Mandates initial one-time mandate registration via compulsory Additional Factor Authentication (AFA). for e-mandates
  • Pre-Debit Customer Alert: Card issuers must transmit pre-transaction debit notifications to the cardholder at least 24 hours prior to account debit.
  • Recurring transactions without: AFA up to ₹15,000; insurance/MF/credit-card bill payments without AFA up to ₹1,00,000
  • No charges may: be levied on customers for e-mandate facility
  • FASTag/NCMC auto-replenish exempted: from pre-transaction notification
🎯 EXAM ANGLE ₹15,000 (general recurring cap) vs ₹1,00,000 (insurance/MF/CC cap) is a strong trap pair.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 13

RBI — NBFC Regulatory Overhaul Cluster (merged: 3-layer proposal, NBFC-UL threshold change, branch authorisation, TReDS)

🪝 Hook — RBI is rewriting the NBFC rulebook on three fronts at once: how NBFCs are layered, how the "upper layer" is defined, and how easily they can open branches.

  • A. Proposed new 3-layer framework (Upper/Middle/Lower) to replace existing 4-layer Scale-Based Regulation (Base/Middle/Upper/Top, Oct 2021)
  • B. Proposed replacing NBFC-UL identification methodology with a flat ₹1 lakh crore asset threshold (vs. current Top-10 + parametric scoring: 70% quantitative, 30% qualitative); to be reviewed every 5 years. Also proposed removing the carve-out that shielded govt-owned NBFCs (NABARD, Exim Bank, SIDBI) from UL classification — aligning to "ownership-neutral regulation"
  • C. NBFC Branch Authorisation, 2026 — NBFCs can open branches without prior RBI approval based on Net Owned Funds (NOF) & credit rating thresholds (₹50 crore NOF / AA rating benchmark)
  • D. Proposed dropping due-diligence requirement for MSMEs onboarding TReDS (Trade Receivables Discounting System)

⏰ Status flag → All four are draft/proposed as of April 2026 — check for finalisation before exam.

🎯 EXAM ANGLE ₹1 lakh crore NBFC-UL threshold is the standout figure across this cluster.

DISPATCH № 26

India's 100 GW Nuclear Power Roadmap by 2047

🪝 Hook — India wants to go from 8.8 GW to 100 GW of nuclear power in 21 years — but first it needs to cut approval timelines almost in half.

  • Long-Term Nuclear Target: Ambition to expand nuclear power capacity to 100 GW by 2047 from the baseline of 8.8 GW (an over 10-fold expansion).
  • Enabling Statutory Framework: Anchored by the proposed SHANTI Act (Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India).
  • Regulatory Clearance Compression: Slashes statutory nuclear project approval cycles from 13 years down to 8–9 years.
  • Capital Investment Requirement: Total required capital investment estimated at ≥₹20 lakh crore based on an industry baseline of ₹22 crore per MW.

MACRO • FISCAL & TAX № 1

India's Economy — Size, Growth & the Feb 1 Budget (merged: Jan's pre-Budget context + Feb's actual Budget content)

🪝 Hook — India overtook Japan to become the world's 4th-largest economy in January, and a month later Nirmala Sitharaman used her record 9th-consecutive Budget to lock in a falling fiscal deficit and a ₹1,000 crore semiconductor push.

  • Global Economic Milestone: India officially surpassed Japan to become the **world's 4th-largest economy with a GDP of 4.18trillion∗∗,targeting3rdpositionby2030byovertakingGermany(4.18 trillion**, targeting 3rd position by 2030 by overtaking Germany (4.18trillion∗∗,targeting3rdpositionby2030byovertakingGermany(7.3 trillion projected).
  • Quarterly & Annual GDP Trajectory: Real GDP expanded by 8.2% in Q2 FY26 (accelerating from 7.8% in Q1 and 7.4% in Q4 FY25); the National Statistical Office (NSO) 1st Advance Estimates pegged FY26 real GDP growth at 7.4% (₹201.90 lakh crore).
  • Economic Survey 2025-26 Projections: Tabled on January 29 by Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman and authored by CEA V. Anantha Nageswaran; projected FY27 real GDP growth at 6.8%–7.2%; banking health strengthened with Gross NPA at 2.2% and Net NPA at 0.5% (Sep 2025); fiscal deficit projected to decline to 4.4% of GDP in FY26 (down from 9.2% in FY21).
  • Global Agency Forecast Consensus: Multilateral institutions aligned around moderated growth — World Bank projected 6.5%, IMF forecast 6.6%/6.2%, and Moody's projected 6.4%/6.5% (OECD, S&P, ADB, and Fitch projected within a similar 6.3%–6.7% band).
  • Union Budget 2026-27 Record Presentation: Presented on February 1, 2026, marking Nirmala Sitharaman's 9th consecutive Union Budget, setting a new all-time record for consecutive presentations (Morarji Desai retains the record for most Budgets overall at 10, non-consecutive).
  • Institutional & Thematic Blueprint: First Budget prepared in the newly commissioned Kartavya Bhawan; anchored around three core 'Kartavyas' — accelerating economic growth, fulfilling citizen aspirations, and building inclusive development.
  • Fiscal Consolidation & Debt Metrics: Fiscal deficit for FY27 targeted down to 4.3% of GDP (from 4.4% Revised Estimate in FY26); Central Government Debt-to-GDP ratio projected at 55.6% (BE 2026-27) versus 56.1% (RE 2025-26); Capital Expenditure (Capex) hiked 9% to a historic high of ₹12.2 lakh crore (4.4% of GDP).
  • Direct Tax Code Modernisation: Enacted the New Income Tax Act, 2025, effective April 1, 2026, drastically slashing total sections from 819 down to 536 to simplify compliance.
  • Financial Market & Capital Taxation: Securities Transaction Tax (STT) increased on Futures to 0.05% (from 0.02%) and on Options to 0.15%; share buyback taxation revised to 22% for corporate promoters and 30% for non-corporate promoters.
  • Strategic Industrial & Infrastructure Outlays: Launched India Semiconductor Mission (ISM) 2.0 with a ₹1,000 crore FY27 outlay; announced 'Biopharma SHAKTI' (₹10,000 crore), the SME Growth Fund (₹10,000 crore), and 7 new High-Speed Rail corridors (₹16 lakh crore).
  • 16th Finance Commission Devolution: Accepted recommendations of the Commission (chaired by Dr. Arvind Panagariya); retained vertical tax devolution to states at 41% (for 2026-27 to 2030-31); introduced a new 10% weightage for 'Contribution to GDP' (replacing the 2.5% weightage for 'Tax & Fiscal Effort'); total grants to states fixed at ₹9.47 lakh crore.
  • Gender Budgeting Expansion: Gender Budget Statement (GBS) share rose to 9.37% of total budget expenditure (up from 8.86%), with total allocation reaching ₹5.01 lakh crore (+11.55% YoY).

🧠 Mnemonic → "9th, 4.3, 4.4" — 9th consecutive Budget, 4.3% fiscal deficit target, 4.4% capex-to-GDP.

MACRO • FISCAL & TAX № 2

India's Fiscal Deficit Tracking — interim data (Apr-Nov & Apr-Dec 2025)

  • 8-Month Fiscal Deficit (Apr–Nov 2025): India's fiscal deficit reached ₹9.76 lakh crore, representing 62.3% of the full-year Budget Estimate (widened from 52.5% during the corresponding period last year), supported by an RBI dividend transfer to the Centre of ₹2.69 lakh crore.
  • 9-Month Fiscal Turnaround (Apr–Dec 2025): The cumulative deficit narrowed sharply to ₹8.55 lakh crore, or 54.5% of the annual estimate, aided by an extraordinary December fiscal surplus of ₹1.21 trillion generated through quarterly corporate advance-tax inflows.
  • Reconciliation with Annual Budget: This interim high-frequency tracking preceded the Union Budget's FY26 Revised Estimate of 4.4% of GDP, demonstrating how mid-year fiscal compression stabilized the annual fiscal deficit path.

Startup India — Redefinition to Include Deep Tech (Feb)

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 13

RBI (Responsible Business Conduct) Third Amendment Directions, 2026 — Full Lifecycle (Feb draft origin → March draft detail → confirmed final status, merged as single regulatory instrument)

🪝 Hook — One RBI rulebook, three sightings across two months: first as a mis-selling reform, then as a digital-fraud compensation draft, and now — confirmed via live search — a finalised rule with a further-delayed rollout.

  • Genesis & Mis-Selling Definition (Feb Draft): Formulated statutory rules defining financial "mis-selling" for the first time; restricted unsolicited telemarketing and sales calls strictly to the window of 9:00 AM to 6:00 PM; originally slated for implementation on July 1, 2026.
  • Digital Fraud Compensation Architecture (March Draft): Mandated structured financial relief for victims of low-value unauthorized digital transactions (up to ₹50,000 net loss), guaranteeing compensation of 85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is lower.
  • Multi-Party Loss Sharing Formula: For losses below ₹29,412, the 85% payout is apportioned between institutions: RBI bears 65% (funded via Depositor Education and Awareness / DEA Fund), the customer's issuing bank bears 10%, and the beneficiary bank bears 10%.
  • 🔄 Final Notification & Extended Deadline (Live Verified): RBI formally issued final Directions on June 24, 2026, but deferred enforcement to January 1, 2027 (pushed from July 1, 2026); guarantees zero customer liability for bank negligence or immediately reported third-party security compromises, active for a 1-year compensation window.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE The revised mandatory implementation date is January 1, 2027 (deferred from July 1, 2026); compensation cap is 85% of net loss or ₹25,000, whichever is lower.
BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 14

RBI — Acquisition Financing Norms (Feb original reform → March deferral, merged as 🔄 UPDATE)

  • Liberalised Prudential Exposure Norms (Feb Reform): RBI raised the bank exposure ceiling for acquisition financing from the proposed 10% to 20% of Tier-1 capital; permitted commercial banks to fund acquisitions of unlisted target companies (provided target has a net worth ≥₹500 crore, 3-year track record of profitability, and minimum BBB- credit rating).
  • Financing Share & Security Margins: Permissible bank financing share increased to 75% of acquisition value (from 70%), while retaining the debt-equity prudential ceiling at 3:1; raised lending against shares to ₹1 crore (from ₹20 lakh) and IPO financing to ₹1 lakh per borrower.
  • 🔄 Implementation Deferral (March Update): RBI formally deferred implementation from April 1, 2026 to July 1, 2026; widened acquisition financing to include statutory mergers and amalgamations; allowed funding via subsidiaries and Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) backed by mandatory Corporate Guarantees.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE The implementation date deferral from April 1, 2026 to July 1, 2026 is the testable trap; bank exposure cap is 20% of capital and max financing is 75% of transaction value.
KISAN CREDIT CARD № 15

Kisan Credit Card (KCC) — Revised Draft Norms (Feb)

  • Extended Credit Facility Tenure: Proposed extending standard Kisan Credit Card (KCC) facility tenure from 5 years to 6 years, aligning credit availability with longer agricultural crop rotation and farm investment cycles.
  • Collateral Waiver & Credit Standardization: Waived mandatory collateral and margin requirements for farm loans up to ₹2 lakh per borrower; standardised short-duration crop loan tenure at 12 months and long-duration crops at 18 months.
  • Marginal Farmer Credit Line & Origins: Established a dedicated flexible revolving credit band of ₹10,000 to ₹50,000 specifically for marginal farmers owning ≤1 hectare of land; KCC scheme was originally launched in 1998 based on the recommendations of the R.V. Gupta Committee and modeled by NABARD.

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 16

Deposit Insurance — Risk-Based Premium (DICGC) (Feb)

  • Transition to Risk-Sensitive Pricing: Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (DICGC) announced a structural shift from a uniform flat premium of 12 paise per ₹100 of deposits to a risk-based premium model effective April 1, 2026.
  • Graded Premium Slabs: Insured commercial and cooperative banks are categorized across four supervisory risk buckets: Category A (safest) pays 8 paise per ₹100, progressing through Categories B and C, up to Category D paying 12 paise per ₹100.
  • Statutory Protection Limit: Statutory insurance coverage ceiling remains unchanged at ₹5 lakh per depositor per bank (covering both principal and interest across all branches of the same bank).

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 17

RBI — REIT Lending Draft Guidelines (Feb)

  • Bank Financing for Real Estate Investment Trusts: Permitted commercial banks to extend credit facilities to Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs), establishing a dedicated regulatory lending avenue for institutional real estate assets.
  • Prudential Exposure Caps: A bank's total exposure to a single REIT is capped at 10% of the bank's eligible capital base; the aggregate banking system exposure across all lenders to an individual REIT cannot exceed 49% of the REIT's total asset value.
  • Effective Implementation Timeline: The final operational guidelines were scheduled for enforcement effective July 1, 2026.

BANKING • MONETARY POLICY № 18

RBI — January-February 2026, consolidated regulatory sweep (merged: same regulator across both months, grouped by theme rather than by month)

🪝 Hook — Across two months, RBI held the repo rate steady while quietly reshaping bank dividends, MSME lending, deposit insurance, acquisition financing, and even rolling out its first-ever 90-day repo — a genuinely dense two-month regulatory sweep from one institution.

  • Monetary Policy Stance: Held Repo Rate unchanged at 5.25% with a neutral stance through both January and the February MPC review (reconfirmed through August 2026); Feb MPC projected FY26 GDP growth at 7.4% and CPI at ~2.1%.
  • Unprecedented Liquidity Operations: Conducted RBI's first-ever 90-day Variable Rate Repo (VRR) auction for ₹25,000 crore on January 30, 2026 (shattering the previous record tenor of 56 days); formed part of a ₹2.15 lakh crore liquidity package including a $10 billion 3-year USD/INR Buy-Sell Swap and ₹1 lakh crore in Open Market Operation (OMO) purchases.
  • 🔄 Bank Dividend Payout Ceiling Finalised: Replaced the decades-old 40% cap with a graded capital-linked framework finalised in March 2026: maximum dividend payout capped at 75% of Profit After Tax (PAT) for commercial banks maintaining a Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) ratio ≥13.0%, while foreign bank branches may remit up to 80% of net profits.
  • MSME & Priority Sector Lending (PSL) Realignment: Raised the mandatory collateral-free loan ceiling for Micro and Small Enterprises (MSEs) from ₹10 lakh to ₹20 lakh (effective April 1, 2026); corrected Small Finance Bank (SFB) priority sector lending target to 60% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) (correcting a typographical notification error of 75%); proposed a 3-year cooling-off gap for UCB directors after 10 continuous board years.
  • External Commercial Borrowings (ECB) Liberalisation: Raised the automatic ECB borrowing ceiling to the higher of $1 billion or 300% of borrower net worth (up from $750 million), following a record $61 billion raised by Indian corporations in FY25.
  • Institutional MoUs & Governance: Signed bilateral MoU with the European Securities and Markets Authority (ESMA) restoring EU bank access to Indian Central Counterparties (CCPs); signed historic agreement with Delhi Government to act as its debt manager and banker enabling municipal market borrowing; formally recognized FEDAI (Foreign Exchange Dealers' Association of India, est. 1958) as an official SRO.
  • Operational & Technology Infrastructure: Commissioned RBI's 2nd state-of-the-art data centre in Bhubaneswar, Odisha (Tier IV certified, backing up primary Kharghar, Navi Mumbai centre); Digital Payments Index (DPI) rose to 516.76 (Sep 2025) from 465.33; annual gold purchases dipped 94% to 4.02 tonnes in 2025 (8-year low) while total sovereign gold reserves touched a record 880.2 tonnes.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE 5 high-yield anchors: (1) 5.25% repo rate, (2) first-ever 90-day VRR auction, (3) 75% bank dividend payout cap (80% for foreign branches), (4) MSME collateral-free loan doubled to ₹20 lakh, and (5) ECB limit raised to $1 billion.

💼 Interview Q → "Why did RBI need its first-ever 90-day repo in January 2026?" — Advance-tax and GST outflows created an unusually large systemic cash crunch in late January; RBI's previous longest VRR tenor was 56 days, so extending to 90 days (alongside a $10bn FX swap and OMO purchases) reflected the scale of the liquidity gap it needed to bridge before the repo rate's own February review.

100% FDI IN INSURANCE № 22

100% FDI in Insurance — "Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha" Act (Feb)

  • Statutory Enforcement & Core Reform: Formally enacted into law on February 5, 2026, permitting 100% Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) under the automatic route in the insurance sector (except Section 25 prohibiting common executive directorships).

  • Market Penetration Context: Enacted to dramatically scale India's low insurance penetration, currently hovering around 3.7% of GDP compared to the global average of 7.0%.

INDIA-EU FREE TRADE AGREEMENT № 50

India-EU Free Trade Agreement — Negotiations Concluded (Jan 27, 2026)

🪝 Hook — After 18 years of on-and-off talks, India and the EU struck the "Mother of All Deals" — but concluding negotiations and the deal actually entering force are two different milestones, so don't conflate them.

  • Negotiation Breakthrough After 18 Years: Announced at the 16th India-EU Summit in New Delhi; negotiations originally commenced in 2007 under the Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement (BTIA) and formally concluded after 18 years.
  • Macro Market Creation: Forges an integrated economic free-trade zone encompassing 2 billion citizens and generating roughly 25% of aggregate global GDP.
  • Bilateral Tariff Dismantlement: India agreed to slash or eliminate customs tariffs on 96.6% of goods imported from the European Union; the EU granted immediate or phased zero-duty preferential market access for over 99% of Indian exports by trade value.
  • Financial Services Integration: Facilitates reciprocal banking access allowing up to 15 EU bank branch expansions in India, aligned with India's newly liberalized 100% FDI insurance framework.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE 18-year negotiation marathon (2007–2026); creates free-trade zone spanning 2 billion people and 25% of global GDP; tariff elimination on 96.6% of EU goods vs 99%+ of Indian goods.

  • One-Time Tax Compliance Window: Ministry of Finance introduced the Foreign Assets Disclosure Scheme (FAST-DS), 2026, providing an exclusive one-time window for resident taxpayers to disclose previously unreported overseas assets and bank accounts.
  • Statutory Immunity Provisions: Offers immunity from criminal prosecution under the Black Money (Undisclosed Foreign Income and Assets) and Imposition of Tax Act, 2015, upon payment of specified tax rates and reduced penalties.
  • Information Exchange Backing: Powered by automatic data feeds under the OECD Common Reporting Standard (CRS) and the US Foreign Account Tax Compliance Act (FATF/FATCA), ensuring detection of undeclared foreign investments.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE One-time foreign asset compliance window framed under Black Money Act, 2015; backed by OECD Common Reporting Standard data exchanges.
POLICY • FLAGSHIP SCHEMES № 86

Credit Guarantee Scheme for MFIs 2.0 (CGSMFI-2.0) (March)

  • Microfinance Credit Guarantee Enhancement: Ministry of Finance launched CGSMFI 2.0 administered through the National Credit Guarantee Trustee Company (NCGTC), providing up to 75% portfolio credit guarantee cover for commercial loans extended to registered Microfinance Institutions.
  • Prudential Sanction Limits: Maximum loan sanctionable to an MFI capped at 20% of its Assets Under Management (AUM), with tiered aggregate ceilings: ₹100 crore for small MFIs, ₹200 crore for medium MFIs, and ₹1,000 crore for large MFIs.
  • AUM Classification Slabs: Classifies MFIs across three regulatory tiers based on balance sheet size: Small (<₹500 crore AUM), Medium (₹500 crore–₹2,000 crore AUM), and Large (>₹2,000 crore AUM).
🎯 EXAM ANGLE 75% guarantee cover via NCGTC; max loan = 20% of AUM capped at ₹100 Cr (Small), ₹200 Cr (Medium), and ₹1,000 Cr (Large MFIs); AUM cutoffs: <₹500 Cr, ₹500–₹2,000 Cr, >₹2,000 Cr.
POLICY • FLAGSHIP SCHEMES № 87

Regional Connectivity Scheme – Modified UDAN (March)

  • Cabinet Financial Outlay: Union Cabinet approved the revised and modified Regional Connectivity Scheme (RCS) – Modified UDAN with an escalated budgetary outlay of ₹28,840 crore to strengthen last-mile regional air connectivity.
  • Helicopter & Water Aerodrome Focus: Prioritizes underserved remote airstrips, tourist circuits, helicopter services in hilly Himalayan and North-Eastern terrains, and amphibious water aerodrome routes.
  • Viability Gap Funding (VGF) Mechanism: Retains concessional airfare caps for 50% of aircraft seats, subsidized through central and state Viability Gap Funding funded by Regional Connectivity Fund (RCF) levies.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE Modified UDAN budgetary outlay of ₹28,840 crore; prioritizes remote airstrips, heliports in Himalayan/NE terrains, and water aerodromes supported by VGF.
POLICY • FLAGSHIP SCHEMES № 88

IVFRT Scheme Continuation (March)

  • Immigration Modernisation Outlay: Union Cabinet approved the phase continuation of the Immigration, Visa and Foreigners Registration & Tracking (IVFRT) scheme with an upgraded allocation of ₹1,800 crore spanning 2026 to 2031 (escalated from previous outlay of ₹1,364 crore).
  • Core Security Mandate: Executed by the Ministry of Home Affairs and Bureau of Immigration, integrating automated biometrics, electronic visas (e-Visa), and real-time passenger tracking across 108 international immigration checkpoints.
  • Operational Integration: Seamlessly interconnects Indian diplomatic missions abroad, Foreigners Regional Registration Offices (FRROs), immigration checkpoints, and security intelligence agencies.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE IVFRT scheme outlay upgraded to ₹1,800 crore for 2026–2031 (up from ₹1,364 Cr); managed by MHA and Bureau of Immigration across 108 international checkpoints.
POLICY • FLAGSHIP SCHEMES № 89

PM Internship Scheme Expansion (March)

  • Corporate Participation Scale: Ministry of Corporate Affairs announced that 549 top Indian corporations enrolled in the pilot phase of the Prime Minister's Internship Scheme, offering over 1.25 lakh internship opportunities across diverse industrial sectors.
  • Financial Stipend Structure: Beneficiaries receive a monthly financial stipend of ₹5,000 (₹4,500 disbursed by Central Government via DBT, and ₹500 contributed from the corporate entity's CSR budget), along with a one-time incidentals grant of ₹6,000.
  • Eligibility Criteria: Open to Indian youth aged 21 to 24 years who are not engaged in full-time employment or formal education, prioritizing youth from households without government employees or high-tax backgrounds.

Coconut Promotion Scheme, GeM's SWAYATT 7-yr milestone, Bharat Audyogik (March)

  • Integrated Coconut Mission Sanction: Ministry of Agriculture cleared the Integrated Coconut Development Scheme with an outlay of ₹1,250 crore to revitalize senile plantations, combat pest infestations, and expand processing in coastal states.
  • GeM SWAYATT 7-Year Milestone: Government e-Marketplace celebrated the 7th anniversary of SWAYATT (Startups, Women and Youth Advantage Through e-Transactions), having onboarded over 3.5 lakh women-led MSMEs and generating cumulative procurements exceeding ₹45,000 crore.

EXTERNAL FINANCING TO INDIA № 91

External Financing to India — combined cluster

  • Multilateral Development Banking Inflows: Asian Development Bank (ADB) and World Bank committed comprehensive project financing loans totaling $1.85 billion across India's urban transit, clean water, and green energy infrastructure sectors.
  • Bilateral ODA Infrastructure Credit: Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA) formalized 399.78 billion Yen (~₹22,000 crore) in concessional assistance for high-speed rail, dedicated freight corridors, and metro lines.
  • Offshore Sustainable Capital Mobilisation: India's corporate and renewable energy entities mobilized over $4.2 billion via foreign external commercial borrowings (ECB) and offshore green bonds listed at GIFT City's IFSC exchanges.
  • Credit Enhancement & Institutional Backing: Multilateral risk agencies including MIGA provided credit insurance and guarantee covers safeguarding foreign direct investment lines into India's rooftop solar and clean mobility ecosystems.
🎯 EXAM ANGLE JICA ~₹22,000 Cr ODA loan package; ADB/World Bank multilateral project financing lines; rising share of offshore green debt listings in GIFT City.
